## Purpose When profiling Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B + z-lab/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-DFlash, we found the KV cache group_size become 1. This increases build metadata overhead. We found the target model Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B layer buckets are [30 mamba, 10 full]. The DFlash drafter z-lab/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-DFlash adds [5 sliding, 1 full], the added 1 full attention layer that can't merge with the target's 10 full attention layers. The current logic used `min` as the group size [here](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/v0.27.0/vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py#L1245-L1246). `group_size = min([30, 10, 5, 1]) = 1` makes it to split into 46 groups of 1 layer each. So this PR update `_get_kv_cache_groups_uniform_page_size` to exclude buckets with 1 layer from the `min` computation. Result: layers [30 mamba, 10 full, 5 sliding, 1 full] become 10 groups instead of 46 groups. e2e output throughput improves 102% at batch size 1 on H200. ``` Group 0: MambaSpec, layers=5 Group 1: MambaSpec, layers=5 Group 2: MambaSpec, layers=5 Group 3: MambaSpec, layers=5 Group 4: MambaSpec, layers=5 Group 5: MambaSpec, layers=5 Group 6: FullAttentionSpec, layers=5 Group 7: FullAttentionSpec, layers=5 Group 8: SlidingWindowSpec, layers=5 Group 9: FullAttentionSpec, layers=1 ``` Note: This PR does not cause regression for other models. ``` ┌─────────────────────────────────────────┬───────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────┐ │ Model │ Before │ After │ ├─────────────────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────┤ │ Qwen3.6-35B-A3B │ 4 groups (10 layers each) │ 4 groups (unchanged) │ ├─────────────────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────┤ │ Qwen3.6-35B-A3B + DFlash │ 46 groups (1 layer each) │ 10 groups │ ├─────────────────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────┤ │ Qwen3.6-35B-A3B + Eagle │ 41 groups (1 layer each) │ 5 groups │ ├─────────────────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────┤ │ gemma-4-26B-A4B-it (5:1 sw/full) │ 6 groups │ 6 groups (unchanged) │ ├─────────────────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────┤ │ gpt-oss-20b (12 sw + 13 full) │ 2 groups │ 2 groups (unchanged) │ └─────────────────────────────────────────┴───────────────────────────┴────────────────────────────┘ ``` ## Test Plan ``` pytest -s -v tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py ``` ## Test Result Unit tests passed. ## Profiling Profiled Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B + z-lab/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-DFlash on H200. nodes.body: This is definitely an important issue. My issue with this implementation is it ignores the kv padding that gets introduced by grouping and leave that unbounded. I see this PR implements this similar idea with a bound https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/49472

> This is definitely an important issue. My issue with this implementation is it ignores the kv padding that gets introduced by grouping and leave that unbounded. I see this PR implements this similar idea with a bound

@mgoin Thanks for review!

Sorry I missed #49472. After looking at the PR, I see the design is to minimize padding and group count.

I also had some design ideas:

Based on the observation that GDNAttentionMetadataBuilder.build() takes ~900µs and FlashAttentionMetadataBuilder.build() takes ~20µs, having less Mamba groups would have better performance (If it's OK to have more padding for better latency). For example, for [30 mamba, 10 full, 5 sliding, 1 full], group_size=10 might have better performance than group_size=5, because group_size=10 leads to 3 mamba groups vs 6 mamba groups. Therefore having a weighted group cost computation to assign more weights to mamba group may help minimize latency. But this idea needs validation.

Also I noticed changing group size might cause accuracy issue for eagle case. Therefore I thought changing the design would need thorough testing.

So I raised this PR to make it simple and does not touch other cases, in order to quickly unblock the performance issue for DFlash.

Thanks @xyang16 for the PR and @mgoin for the review!
Let's discuss this further. 

Few thoughts:
1. I am surprised that choice of group would at all impact accuracy, that should be looked into imo. 
2. Looking ahead, it is definitely useful to have weighted selection. However, that might be non-reliable and implementation/hardware-dependent. Therefore, I am not sure what the best option would be here.
3. I'd be in favor of having a somewhat okay algorithm that works across multiple cases instead of tailoring it to the current model config. I'm worried that we might have a model come out in the next months that would eg have the following groups: [30, 10, 3, 2]. With this PR, it would result in gs=2, 15 + 5 + 2 + 1 = 23 groups and 1 padding, still too many. With the other PR, we arrive at gs=5, 6 + 2 + 1 + 1 = 10 groups and 5 padding.

Let me know what you think.

Agreed this is an important issue. 

> Based on the observation that GDNAttentionMetadataBuilder.build() takes ~900µs 

QQ: I am not quite familiar with GDN metadata builder but 900us does look too long. Should we instead optimize this part, in addition to fix the grouping issue here?

> Agreed this is an important issue.
> 
> > Based on the observation that GDNAttentionMetadataBuilder.build() takes ~900µs
> 
> QQ: I am not quite familiar with GDN metadata builder but 900us does look too long. Should we instead optimize this part, in addition to fix the grouping issue here?

@ivanium Yes. I have raised https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52078 and https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52297 that reduce the GDN metadata build from ~900us to ~300us. Could you please take a look? Thanks.

detail.title: [Spec Decode] Fix KV cache group explosion for hybrid models

files.patch:
@@ -1208,9 +1208,15 @@ def _get_kv_cache_groups_uniform_page_size(
     # is the minimum number of layers among all attention types. Need a better
     # strategy if we want to support more complex patterns (e.g., 20 full + 30
     # sw, where the group size should be 10).
-    min_num_layers = min([len(layers) for layers in layer_buckets])
+    bucket_sizes = [len(layers) for layers in layer_buckets]
+    multi_layer_sizes = [s for s in bucket_sizes if s > 1]
+
+    # Singleton buckets can be introduced by speculative drafters such as DFlash.
+    # Do not let such outliers force the group size to 1, which can significantly
+    # increase the number of KV cache groups.
+    min_num_layers = min(multi_layer_sizes) if multi_layer_sizes else 1
     group_size = min_num_layers
-    max_num_layers = max([len(layers) for layers in layer_buckets])
+    max_num_layers = max(bucket_sizes)
     if max_num_layers < min_num_layers * 1.5:
         # If the number of layers is not much larger than the minimum number of
         # layers, use the maximum number of layers as the group size to avoid

issue_comments.body: This is definitely an important issue. My issue with this implementation is it ignores the kv padding that gets introduced by grouping and leave that unbounded. I see this PR implements this similar idea with a bound https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/49472

> This is definitely an important issue. My issue with this implementation is it ignores the kv padding that gets introduced by grouping and leave that unbounded. I see this PR implements this similar idea with a bound

@mgoin Thanks for review!

Sorry I missed #49472. After looking at the PR, I see the design is to minimize padding and group count.

I also had some design ideas:

Based on the observation that GDNAttentionMetadataBuilder.build() takes ~900µs and FlashAttentionMetadataBuilder.build() takes ~20µs, having less Mamba groups would have better performance (If it's OK to have more padding for better latency). For example, for [30 mamba, 10 full, 5 sliding, 1 full], group_size=10 might have better performance than group_size=5, because group_size=10 leads to 3 mamba groups vs 6 mamba groups. Therefore having a weighted group cost computation to assign more weights to mamba group may help minimize latency. But this idea needs validation.

Also I noticed changing group size might cause accuracy issue for eagle case. Therefore I thought changing the design would need thorough testing.

So I raised this PR to make it simple and does not touch other cases, in order to quickly unblock the performance issue for DFlash.

Thanks @xyang16 for the PR and @mgoin for the review!
Let's discuss this further. 

Few thoughts:
1. I am surprised that choice of group would at all impact accuracy, that should be looked into imo. 
2. Looking ahead, it is definitely useful to have weighted selection. However, that might be non-reliable and implementation/hardware-dependent. Therefore, I am not sure what the best option would be here.
3. I'd be in favor of having a somewhat okay algorithm that works across multiple cases instead of tailoring it to the current model config. I'm worried that we might have a model come out in the next months that would eg have the following groups: [30, 10, 3, 2]. With this PR, it would result in gs=2, 15 + 5 + 2 + 1 = 23 groups and 1 padding, still too many. With the other PR, we arrive at gs=5, 6 + 2 + 1 + 1 = 10 groups and 5 padding.

Let me know what you think.

Agreed this is an important issue. 

> Based on the observation that GDNAttentionMetadataBuilder.build() takes ~900µs 

QQ: I am not quite familiar with GDN metadata builder but 900us does look too long. Should we instead optimize this part, in addition to fix the grouping issue here?

> Agreed this is an important issue.
> 
> > Based on the observation that GDNAttentionMetadataBuilder.build() takes ~900µs
> 
> QQ: I am not quite familiar with GDN metadata builder but 900us does look too long. Should we instead optimize this part, in addition to fix the grouping issue here?

@ivanium Yes. I have raised https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52078 and https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52297 that reduce the GDN metadata build from ~900us to ~300us. Could you please take a look? Thanks.
